genZNote: No envelope means it shrugs off stomach acid on the way to the gut — exactly how a fecal-oral virus needs to travel.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human gastrointestinal tract — humans are the only natural host and reservoir
habitat.hostAssociation: Infects the GI epithelium and can spread to the central nervous system via the bloodstream
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans, including asymptomatic carriers who shed virus in stool

identificationClues: Diagnosed by viral culture or RT-PCR of stool or throat swab specimens
Non-enveloped +ssRNA virus — resistant to gastric acid and bile, enabling fecal-oral transmission and GI survival
Most infections are asymptomatic or cause mild, self-limited illness; a small percentage progress to aseptic meningitis or flaccid paralysis
Global eradication efforts (oral and inactivated polio vaccines) have eliminated wild poliovirus from nearly all countries

diseases: Poliomyelitis — ranges from asymptomatic infection (most common) to non-paralytic aseptic meningitis to paralytic disease from destruction of anterior horn motor neurons, causing asymmetric flaccid paralysis
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route; also possible via respiratory droplets early in infection
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Once a major cause of childhood paralysis worldwide; global vaccination efforts (Global Polio Eradication Initiative) have eliminated wild-type poliovirus from all but a small number of countries
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Stool viral culture remains the reference standard for confirming poliovirus infection, supplemented by RT-PCR and genomic sequencing to distinguish wild-type from vaccine-derived strains

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by viral culture/RT-PCR
examFacts.importantDisease: Poliomyelitis — asymmetric flaccid paralysis from anterior horn cell destruction
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A non-enveloped +ssRNA enterovirus whose gastric-acid resistance underlies fecal-oral spread, with paralysis resulting from destruction of anterior horn motor neurons
